basicMistakes.where: With the brief's own sample values the card shows only FIGHT NIGHT, VS and the RED CORNER / BLUE CORNER labels. No boxer names, gym logos, records or weight class appear on either side. G-3 and G-16/G-17 are the same.
Select winner leaves the board exactly as it was. No winner is marked on either side, at 1500 ms or at 10000 ms (G-23).
Lock it in after Select winner only fades in a yellow centre rule. No locked winner is shown on either side. G-28 (lock with no selection) is also unchanged.
Blue corner name wrapped onto two lines with very tight line spacing: the accent on the Á in PHÁDRAIG pushes up into the line above, under SÚILLEABHÁIN (also visible in G-4/G-10).
Updating the red boxer's name shows only the name. The red side's gym and record line never appears, and the blue side stays completely empty.

missingActions: select (no winner state is ever shown)
lock (no locked-winner state is ever shown)
otherProblems: The dark blue-on-black gym crest sits on its own white rounded plate on the blue side, while the white crest on the red side sits bare. The two logos are treated differently and the plate looks like an accident.
The bottom quarter of the card and the area above the corner labels are huge empty colour fields. The content is crammed low in each half and the top half carries nothing.
The rule in the middle fades in from yellow to transparent and reads as a smudge rather than a designed divider.
The two sides get unequal vertical treatment when one name wraps: the blue name drops to two lines and pushes its record line lower than the red one.
answer.reasons: This card can't go on air. With the brief's own sample values it shows nothing but the title, VS and the two corner labels: no boxers, logos, records or weight class. The winner steps don't work either. Select and clear change nothing on screen, and lock only fades in a yellow centre line, so the decision is never shown. Even with the long stress values, where the content does appear, the wrapped Irish name crowds its accent into the line above, and the dark logo sits on a white plate that doesn't match the bare white logo on the red side.

otherProblems: With the long category value, the title shrinks and wraps to two lines (G-5 to G-7, G-34 to G-38). It is clean but has less presence than the short title.
The Suspense state only dims the nominees slightly (G-17 to G-22), so it's a weak visual cue for building suspense.
After Reveal, the losing nominees are dimmed hard (G-27/G-28). They are still legible, but their film titles are quite faint.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board with a double gold frame, a monospaced kicker, a bold category title, a short gold rule and four evenly spaced name/title pairs. It stays solid and readable over the dark stage, the bright plate and the busy plate. Long names and the long category wrap cleanly inside the panel and never collide or clip. Suspense dims the field and Reveal puts the winner in a framed gold highlight while the other nominees recede. Both required actions work, and the Take, Update and Out transitions stay tidy. Nothing a viewer would see keeps it off air.

otherProblems: Sample state (G-2/G-3/G-4 and every operator-step frame): the 880px-wide panel holds only a small label and 'Anonymous' in its left third; the right ~60% is empty dark slab, so the alert reads as unfinished.
A faint orange hairline sits alone at the bottom right of the panel (G-2, G-5, G-8 and others). It is attached to nothing and looks like an accident rather than a timer bar.

Long stress value (G-5/G-6/G-7, crop G-69): the username wraps mid-word as 'xX_Ångström_Gänseblümche' / 'n_Xx'. Breaking a name between letters looks clumsy on air; it should be scaled, ellipsised or broken at the underscore.
The amount, which is the key fact of a donation alert, is set as small grey monospace tucked after the event label (G-5, crop G-71). It is the weakest element on the panel.
The white avatar shield is cropped at the top and bottom by its circular ring (crop G-72), so it looks jammed into the frame.
The empty-values state (G-8/G-9/G-10) leaves a lone 'DONATION' label floating mid-height in an otherwise empty band.
Hold and Resume look the same on screen, and the alert is still up at 10 s with or without Hold (G-16, G-22, G-28). Nothing tells the operator whether the timer is running.
answer.reasons: There are no hard failures: text never overlaps, contrast holds on all three backgrounds, nothing spills out of the panel, and the surface offers skip, replay, hold and resume. The design is the problem. In the sample state, which is what goes on air most of the time, a very wide dark bar holds a small label and a name crammed into its left edge, plus a stray hairline at the far right. The long name breaks mid-word, the amount is the smallest and dimmest text on the panel, and the white avatar is clipped by its ring. Each fix is small, but together they make it a graphic that "would work with a few tweaks", not one that airs today.

otherProblems: With the brief's own values (G-2 to G-4, and the Take, Hold, Resume, Replay and Next frames) the alert shows only 'DONATION / Anonymous' and a placeholder '+' avatar. It never shows an amount or a message, although the brief asks for both.
The panel is about 880 px wide, but in every sample frame the kicker and name fill only the left third. The right two thirds are an empty dark slab, so the alert looks broken rather than designed.
In G-5 to G-7 the long username wraps mid-word with no hyphen ('xX_Ǎngström_Gänseblümche' / 'n_Xx'). The 'Å' also renders like a caron. A viewer would read it as a broken name.
The donation amount (€25.00) is small grey monospaced text tucked into the kicker line. In a donation alert the amount should stand out.
A faint orange hairline floats at the bottom-right corner of the panel in every frame. It is tied to nothing and looks accidental.
The white shield avatar in G-5 and G-72 fills its ring edge to edge, with no breathing room.
answer.reasons: Nothing is clipped, the contrast holds on all three grounds, and all four operator actions (skip, replay, hold, resume) are on the surface. But with the brief's own values the alert never shows an amount or a message. The content sits in the left third of a wide panel that is otherwise empty. The stress username breaks mid-word, the amount is buried in small grey type, and a stray hairline sits in the corner. A director would send this back rather than air it.

basicMistakes.where: Donor name, first line, top right panel: the ring of 'Å' in 'xX_Ångström' is cut off at the top of the line box and reads as 'Ǎ'. The same cut shows in G-6, G-7 and the G-69 crop.

otherProblems: The long username wraps mid-word with no hyphen ('Gänseblümche' / 'n_Xx'), splitting the name awkwardly across two lines (G-5, G-6, G-7).

With the sample values (G-2 to G-4), DONATION / Anonymous sits in the left third of a fixed ~880 px panel and the rest of the panel is empty dark space, so the text looks pushed into a corner. With empty values (G-8 to G-10) the panel holds only the word DONATION.
A thin gold hairline floats alone in the bottom-right corner of the panel. It never visibly changes, even across the 10-second hold, so it reads as a stray mark rather than a timer.
The panel is semi-transparent, so on the busy ground the blue blob shows through behind the name and message (G-7). The text is still readable, but it looks muddy.
answer.reasons: The operator surface offers all four actions the brief asks for: skip clears the alert, replay re-runs it, and hold and resume both behave. The long value fails, though. The 'Å' in the umlaut-heavy username loses the top of its ring and reads as 'Ǎ', and the name breaks mid-word across two lines, which is exactly the case the brief warned about. With normal values the alert is a wide, mostly empty bar with the text crammed to the left, and a stray gold hairline sits in the corner. It is clean and readable in places, but a director would send it back before air.

basicMistakes.where: Whole card with the brief's sample values: only FIGHT NIGHT, VS and the RED/BLUE CORNER labels appear. No boxer names, gym logos, records or weight class are shown. The same holds for G-3 and G-12 to G-57.
Select winner: the card is unchanged and no winner is ever marked on either side (also G-23, G-50, G-51).

missingActions: select (no winner indication is ever visible)
otherProblems: The blue corner's dark gym logo sits on a white rounded square plate, while the red logo sits directly on the panel. The two logos are treated inconsistently, and one is a logo on a box of its own.
In the long-values frames the content sits at different heights on the two sides: the record lines don't align across the card (KAUNAS line at about y930, ST. MICHAEL'S at about y940).
The upper half of each corner is a huge empty field of flat colour, so the card reads as unfinished.
In G-13 the transition flashes a near-empty card in which FIGHT NIGHT is half-faded and unreadable.
answer.reasons: G would not go on air. With the brief's own sample values the card never shows the boxers, logos, records or weight class. It is just two coloured halves with the corner labels and VS. The operator surface lists select, lock and clear, but pressing select or lock never shows a winner. Only the long-value frames fill in the content, and even there a diacritic in the wrapped Irish name collides with the line above and the blue logo sits on a white plate. The core job of the brief, a filled face-off card with a winner call, is not delivered.

basicMistakes.where: Whole card with the brief's sample values: only FIGHT NIGHT, VS and the RED CORNER / BLUE CORNER labels appear. No boxer names, gym logos, records or weight class on either side. G-3, G-16 and G-17 look the same.

answer.reasons: This would not go on air. With the brief's own sample values, the full-frame card shows only the corner labels and a VS badge. There are no boxers, logos, records or weight class, so the card's main job never happens. Select winner and Lock it in produce no visible winner state in any frame, so the post-decision part of the brief is missing too. Even when names do render (the long-value frames), the blue logo sits on an odd white plate and the two-line Irish name nearly collides with itself. Several single-side frames also leave one corner completely blank.

otherProblems: In the long-value frames (G-5 to G-7) the category drops to a two-line heading in smaller type than the nominee names, so the title of the board reads weaker than its entries.
Long names wrap to a second line inside a narrow centre column even though the panel has plenty of room either side. This leaves single-word lines such as 'Fitzgerald' and 'DIRECTOR'.
The reveal marks the winner only with a gold-outlined box and gold name, with no 'Winner' label. It is clear, but understated for an awards moment.
answer.reasons: G airs. It is a clean, centred black-and-gold board with a gold double frame, a small gold kicker, a bold category and four director-and-film pairs in clear cream and gold. The solid black panel keeps all text readable over the dark, light and busy backgrounds. Long names and titles wrap cleanly inside the panel, with nothing clipped or overlapping. Suspense dims the field and reveal lifts the winner into a gold-outlined box while the others recede, so both operator actions are present and work. The category update reflows neatly, and the take and out animations are tidy. The empty state shows only the category over a mostly empty panel, but that is a state with no data. The remaining issues are small typographic choices, not errors a viewer would see.

otherProblems: With the long values, the category title wraps to two lines at a much smaller size than the nominee names (G-5 to G-7, G-34 to G-38), so the title loses its rank in the hierarchy.
Long director names wrap at the hyphen ('Okonkwo- / Fitzgerald', 'Vasconcelos- / Albuquerque'), so the line breaks look a little uneven.
The suspense state only dims the nominee names slightly (G-17 to G-22), which is a subtle cue for a big moment.
The winner's highlight box hugs its text, with tight top and bottom padding (G-25 to G-28).
answer.reasons: This airs. The centred black-and-gold board has a solid near-black plate, so the cream and gold text reads cleanly over the video, light and busy grounds. The long names and titles wrap inside the frame without clipping. The surface offers suspense and reveal, and the reveal clearly marks the winner with a gold-framed box while the other nominees dim. The Take, the category update and the Out all run cleanly. The few weaknesses (a shrunken long category title, hyphen line breaks, a subtle suspense state) are small nits a viewer would hardly notice, not faults that keep it off air.
